Careers in Finance: Core Roles, Day-to-Day Work & What It Takes to Crack Them

Most students treat "finance" as a single job title. In reality, Indian capital markets and corporate finance are divided into distinct analytical tracks—each testing different technical skills, regulatory certifications, and portfolio deliverables in interviews.

By Harion Research · Comprehensive Student & Graduate Guide · 15 min read

00 / Quick Comparison Matrix

The 6 Core Finance Career Tracks in India

Before preparing for interviews, understand what each desk actually does and what proof of work hiring managers look for on a fresher or intern resume:

1. Equity Research Analyst Institutional Brokerages (Sell-Side), Mutual Funds / PMS / AIFs (Buy-Side), Global Capability Centres (GCCs) Reading annual reports (Ind AS), 3-statement financial modelling, sector benchmarking, DCF & relative valuation NISM Series XV CFA L1/L2 2–3 complete 10–15 page company research reports + Excel financial models on listed NSE/BSE stocks

Role 01 · Capital Markets Core

1. Equity Research Analyst (Sell-Side, Buy-Side & Global Research Centres)

Equity research is the foundational analytical role in capital markets. Every other desk—whether portfolio management, investment banking, or institutional sales—relies on the industry notes, financial models, and company reports produced by equity research analysts.

What the job actually involves day to day

  • Reading primary filings: Studying 300-page annual reports, quarterly results, investor presentations, earnings call transcripts, and DRHPs of listed companies within a designated sector (e.g., Pharmaceuticals, IT Services, Industrials, Chemicals, or BFSI).
  • Maintaining financial models: Updating three-statement Excel models (Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow Statement) after every quarterly earnings release, tracking volume growth, realization, raw-material margins, and working-capital days.
  • Sector & channel tracking: Monitoring raw-material price indices, regulatory notifications, import/export data, and competitor capacity expansions.
  • Writing research reports: Authoring initiation reports, quarterly result updates, and sector thematic notes that clearly lay out business economics, valuation sensitivities, and key risks.

Where freshers get hired in India

Entry-level analysts typically start in one of three places: Sell-Side Institutional Brokerages (where you assist a senior lead analyst covering 10–15 stocks in a sector), Buy-Side Research Teams at Mutual Funds (AMCs), Portfolio Management Services (PMS), and Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), or Global Capability Centres (GCCs) & Research KPOs in Mumbai, Bengaluru, Gurugram, Pune, Hyderabad, and Indore that support global institutional desks.

What is required to crack Equity Research interviews

  • Must-Have TechnicalsInd AS financial statement linkages, DuPont ROE/ROCE decomposition, working-capital cash conversion (OCF vs. EBITDA), DCF & peer multiples (P/E, EV/EBITDA, P/B).
  • CertificationsNISM-Series-XV (Research Analyst Certification) is mandatory for SEBI-registered analyst roles; CFA Level 1/2 is a strong plus.
  • The Interview TestHiring managers will ask: "Pitch or walk me through one listed company you have researched in depth." Candidates who bring a printed 12-page research report and their own 5-year Excel model immediately stand out from 95% of applicants.
  • How to Prepare at HarionEquity Research Internship Program (60 days, 40 classroom lessons free + weekly mentor review) & Market Analysis Learning Lab.
Role 02 · Asset Allocation & Risk

2. Portfolio Management & Institutional Wealth Research

While an equity research analyst studies individual companies and sectors in depth, a portfolio management analyst studies how multiple assets and stocks behave together inside a portfolio.

What the job actually involves day to day

  • Portfolio construction & sizing: Determining how capital is allocated across asset classes (equities, fixed income, gold, cash) and across capitalization segments (large, mid, and small cap) based on an investor mandate's risk profile.
  • Risk & drawdown monitoring: Tracking portfolio volatility, sector concentration limits, beta, maximum drawdown, and liquidity constraints across market regimes.
  • Performance attribution: Evaluating whether historical performance came from sector allocation or individual security selection compared against benchmarks like NIFTY 50 or NIFTY 500.
  • Rebalancing frameworks: Designing rule-based schedules for trimming over-extended positions and rebalancing back to target weights.

What is required to crack Portfolio & Wealth roles

  • Must-Have TechnicalsCAGR vs. XIRR, standard deviation, maximum drawdown, Sharpe & Sortino ratios, correlation across asset classes, and behavioural biases in market cycles.
  • CertificationsNISM Series V-A (Mutual Fund Distributors), NISM Series XXI-A (PMS), NISM Series X-A/X-B (Investment Adviser), or CFA.
  • The Interview Test"How would you construct and monitor a multi-sector portfolio across a trending market versus a volatile drawdown phase?"
  • How to Prepare at HarionPortfolio Manager Program (8 weeks, guided case studies on asset allocation, drawdown control and rebalancing).
Role 03 · Deals, M&A & Capital Raising

3. Investment Banking (IBD), Valuations & Deal Advisory

Investment banking and transaction advisory teams advise corporations on raising capital (IPOs, QIPs, private equity) and executing mergers, acquisitions, or restructurings.

What the job actually involves day to day

  • Comparable company & transaction spreads: Compiling trading multiples (EV/Revenue, EV/EBITDA, P/E) of listed peer companies and precedent M&A transaction multiples.
  • Valuation modelling: Building multi-scenario Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) models, sensitivity matrices (WACC vs. terminal growth), and Net Asset Value (NAV) schedules.
  • Information Memorandums & Pitchbooks: Drafting detailed industry landscapes, buyer/investor shortlists, and company positioning decks.
  • Financial due diligence support: Assisting in reviewing historical quality of earnings, working-capital normalization, and net debt adjustments.

What is required to crack Investment Banking & Valuation roles

  • Must-Have TechnicalsEnterprise Value vs. Equity Value bridge, Free Cash Flow to Firm (FCFF) vs. Free Cash Flow to Equity (FCFE), WACC calculation, Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM), and accounting adjustments.
  • Common Interview Questions"If depreciation increases by ₹100 Crore, walk me through the exact impact on all three financial statements." / "Why do we subtract cash and add debt when computing Enterprise Value?"
  • Proof of Work NeededA clean, zero-error 3-statement financial model and valuation sensitivity workbook built from an Indian company's annual report.
Role 04 · Solvency, Debt & Downside Analysis

4. Credit Research, Rating Agencies & Corporate Banking

Credit analysts at rating agencies (such as CRISIL, ICRA, CARE, and India Ratings) and commercial/corporate banks evaluate a company's ability and willingness to service its debt obligations on time. It is one of the best training grounds in India for learning deep balance-sheet and cash-flow forensics.

What the job actually involves day to day

  • Cash-flow waterfall & solvency analysis: Studying whether Cash Flow from Operations (CFO) is sufficient to cover working-capital needs, scheduled term-loan repayments, and interest expenses across industry downturns.
  • Working-capital & audit scrutiny: Examining receivable ageing schedules, inventory buildup, bank-line utilization, CARO auditor remarks, related-party loans, and contingent liabilities.
  • Writing rating rationales & credit memos: Drafting structured credit notes detailing business risk profile, industry cyclicality, management track record, and financial risk profile.

What is required to crack Credit Analyst interviews

  • Must-Have TechnicalsDebt-to-Equity, Total Debt / EBITDA, Interest Coverage Ratio, Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR), Current Ratio, Cash Conversion Cycle, and reading Notes to Accounts.
  • The Interview Test"A manufacturing company reports growing net income, but its operating cash flow is negative for two consecutive years. What lines on the balance sheet will you check first?"
  • Relevant Study CaseRead our sample case study: Evaluating Balance-Sheet Leverage and Interest Coverage Across Market Phases.
Role 05 · Market Structure & Derivatives

5. Derivatives Dealing, Risk Management & Quantitative Study Desks

Exchange-traded derivatives (index and stock futures and options) represent a major share of Indian capital market turnover. Brokerages, institutional execution desks, clearing members, and risk teams hire analysts who understand contract mechanics, payoff math, and exchange risk rules.

What the job actually involves day to day

  • Derivatives pricing & hedging mechanics: Understanding cost-of-carry in futures, basis risk, beta hedging of equity portfolios, and option payoff structures.
  • Monitoring Greeks & margins: Tracking Delta, Gamma, Theta, Vega, implied volatility, open-interest concentration, SPAN margin, exposure margin, and daily mark-to-market (MTM) settlement obligations.
  • Rule-based historical observation: Studying price, volume, and volatility regimes systematically across NSE and BSE universes without emotional bias.

What is required to crack Derivatives & Market Structure roles

  • Must-Have TechnicalsFutures hedging math, option spread payoffs (breakeven, max loss, max gain), put-call parity, Option Greeks, and SEBI clearing/margin regulations.
  • Mandatory CertificationNISM-Series-VIII (Equity Derivatives Certification Examination) is mandatory for approved users at broking and derivatives desks in India.
  • How to Prepare at HarionNISM Series VIII Preparation (30 days, live doubt sessions 2x/week + 3 full scored mock exams) & NISM VIII Study Guide.
Role 06 · Inside Operating Businesses

6. Corporate Finance, FP&A & Treasury

Every listed and large unlisted company in India has an internal finance team responsible for Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), capital budgeting, investor relations, and treasury management.

What the job actually involves day to day

  • Annual operating plans & variance analysis: Building plant-level or business-unit budgets and analyzing monthly actual vs. budgeted revenue, raw-material cost, and EBITDA margin variances.
  • Capex & unit-economics evaluation: Modelling whether a new factory line, warehouse, or product launch meets internal Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) and payback thresholds.
  • Competitor benchmarking: Tracking quarterly filings of listed sector competitors to brief the CFO and board on relative margin and working-capital performance.
07 / The Preparation Blueprint

How to Crack Finance Roles as a Student in India (4-Step Roadmap)

Across all six career tracks above, recruiters filter out resumes that list only generic college degrees or passive webinar certificates. To crack interviews consistently, follow this four-step sequence:

  1. STEP 01 Master Filings Learn to read real Indian Annual Reports (MD&A, CARO, 3 statements & Notes to Accounts).
  2. STEP 02 Screen Data Use the Harion Research Scanner to compare sectors, ROCE, margins & leverage across NSE/BSE.
  3. STEP 03 Build Proof Complete the 60-day Internship to build your own 5-year model & research report.
  4. STEP 04 Get Certified Pair your report portfolio with NISM Series XV (Research) or NISM Series VIII (Derivatives).
